title: Mosaic: Runtime-Efficient Multi-Agent Embodied Planning
claim: Naive multi-agent execution wastes time through spatially invalid and uncoordinated actions, causing failures and idle agents.
layout: 2 agent columns, top-to-bottom timeline, yellow callouts pointing at failed steps
description: A concrete failure case for the task 'Locate and Rescue a Person'. Two tall gray rounded panels, Agent A and Agent B, each hold a vertical stack of six action boxes read top to bottom. A central arrow labeled Time runs down between them, and a bracket labeled Actions sits on the far left. Boxes are color-coded green for successful actions, red for failed actions and white for no action. Agent A mostly waits (white Wait/No-op boxes) and then fails at Carry(Person) before succeeding at step 6. Agent B fails twice at NavigateTo(Person), picks up debris, fails Carry(Person), drops debris, then succeeds. Three yellow speech-bubble callouts on the right point to the red boxes. They name two spatial failures (target unreachable due to debris, repeated navigation) and one unsatisfied precondition (hands occupied). A legend at the bottom explains the colors. The eye goes first to the red boxes and the yellow callouts.
caption: Multi-agent task execution showing failures driven by spatial and coordination inefficiencies. These inefficiencies also induce agent underutilization during stalled periods.
abstract: LLM-based multi-agent embodied planning remains impractical due to prohibitively high execution latency. We identify failed actions as the dominant bottleneck, stemming from two core challenges: inaccurate state tracking under partial observability and inefficient coordination that produces redundant or conflicting actions. We introduce Mosaic, a runtime-efficient multi-agent planning framework that addresses both challenges. Mosaic maintains accurate yet lightweight state tracking through agent-centric semantic memory that stores objects in relative coordinates, enabling geometric transformations and coordination. It ensures efficient coordination through Integer Linear Programming that allocates actions at every planning step, enforcing physical feasibility and inter-agent coordination constraints. Across AI2-THOR and search-and-rescue benchmarks, Mosaic achieves 27-32% faster execution, 30-33% fewer LLM calls, 25-31% fewer steps, and 4-10% points higher success rates. These results demonstrate that efficient memory and constraint-guided coordination are critical for scalable, low-latency multi-agent planning.
